hypothesis: Honey bees, vespid wasps, and caterpillars (Lepidoptera) become a motionless, hardened pupal stage after the larva is full grown, and the adult emerges from that stage.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. SUPPORTS if the Animal Diversity Web accounts of Apis mellifera, Vespula vulgaris, and Danaus plexippus each describe a pupa or chrysalis that is immobile, motionless, quiescent, or non-feeding, and from which the adult emerges or which lies between the larva and the adult.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if any of the three accounts describes development from larva to adult with no pupal stage. MIXED if the pupal description holds for one or two of the three taxa only. INCONCLUSIVE with reason data-unavailable if an account cannot be fetched or its text does not mention development or metamorphosis at all for a taxon, so that fewer than three taxa can be scored and the scored ones do not already refute. iNaturalist life-stage annotation counts for the pupal stage are recorded and do not decide the verdict.

test_contract.expected_observation: Bees, wasps, and a butterfly each have a non-feeding or immobile pupa between larva and adult.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Any of those three develops from larva to adult without a pupa.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public life-cycle accounts of Apis mellifera, Vespula vulgaris, and Danaus plexippus. Danaus stands in for caterpillars (Lepidoptera), the group named in the claim. iNaturalist annotations are corroborative counts only.
test_contract.inference_method: Phrase match on stripped account text. A taxon passes only if a pupa or chrysalis is named and an immobility or non-feeding phrase is present and the adult is described as following that stage. All three taxa must pass to support.

interpretation: Aristotle's 'scolex' is read as the larva, and the motionless hardened stage as the pupa of holometabolous insects. The claim is tested on the three groups he names (bees, wasps, caterpillars), not on insects that lack complete metamorphosis. 'A sort of egg' is the pupal comparison, not a claim that the pupa is an unfertilized egg.

datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web life cycles of Apis mellifera, Vespula maculifrons, and Danaus plexippus
datasets.role: development prose for a bee, a vespid wasp, and a butterfly

method: The Development section of each account was isolated. A taxon passes when that section names a pupa, pupation, or chrysalis, and a hardened-covering word (cocoon, chrysalis, sealed cell, or case) shares that sentence. The adult counts when emerge/adult appears in that sentence or in the next two. 'Adult workers' sealing a cell does not count. Nest-building mentions of cocoon silk do not count.

measured.unit: of three groups (bee, vespid wasp, butterfly) whose development text describes an enclosed pupa

stage_sentences: Honeybees are holometabolous insects, and have four stages in the life cycle: egg, larva, pupa, and adult.
At the end of that period their cell is sealed by adult workers, and the larva molts, spins a silk cocoon, and transforms into the pupa stage.
husk_sentences: At the end of that period their cell is sealed by adult workers, and the larva molts, spins a silk cocoon, and transforms into the pupa stage.
adult_sentences: Once their final metamorphosis is complete, they chew their way out of the cell and begin their adult life.

stage_sentences: Once they have grown large enough they pupate.
Eventually each caterpillar stops growing and forms a case around itself called a chrysalis.
Inside the chrysalis it changes its body its body in a process called metamorphosis.
husk_sentences: Eventually each caterpillar stops growing and forms a case around itself called a chrysalis.
Inside the chrysalis it changes its body its body in a process called metamorphosis.
adult_sentences: When it is done it emerges as an adult butterfly.

deviations.what_changed: The wasp account and the immobility phrase list.
deviations.why: The pre-registered Vespula vulgaris page is a classification stub with no Development section, so it cannot be scored. Vespula maculifrons, a vespid wasp, was substituted. The adjectives immobile, motionless, quiescent, and non-feeding do not occur in these accounts. A sealed cell, a silk cocoon, or a chrysalis case, in a sentence that names the pupa, was accepted as the hardened husk. The threshold is still all three groups. iNaturalist counts stay non-decisive.

deviations.what_changed: An emergence phrase counts in the stage-and-husk sentence or in the next two sentences.
deviations.why: The pre-registered rule says the adult follows the pupal stage. On the monarch account the chrysalis sentence and the emergence sentence are one sentence apart, so requiring both in a single sentence dropped a description the criterion already accepts. The covering word must still share a sentence with the stage name. The phrase 'adult workers' is not read as the emerging adult.

headline: 2 of 3 groups have an enclosed pupa in the fetched development text (Apis mellifera:pass, Vespula maculifrons:not, Danaus plexippus:pass).
caveats: The word motionless is not in the accounts. The husk is scored from cocoon, sealed cell, or chrysalis.
Vespula maculifrons says the larva pupates and the adult emerges. That sentence does not name a shell, so the wasp does not pass.
iNaturalist annotation counts, when retrieved, are not part of the verdict.
